newsitem.title: FRANCE: French parliament gives Jospin vote of confidence.
newsitem.headline: French parliament gives Jospin vote of confidence.

text.p: New French Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin won a vote of confidence from the National Assembly for his maiden policy statement on Thursday.
A comfortable majority of 297 deputies voted for the coalition government of Socialists, Communists and ecologists, 252 voted against and 2 abstained.
Just one member of the leftist majority withheld support. Hardline Communist deputy Maxime Gremetz abstained, saying Jospin's programme "is not going in the right direction".

Socialist floor leader Jean-Marc Ayrault, pledging support to the new government, praised Jospin's caution, saying "nothing would be more dangerous and more fallacious than an avalanche of measures and bills, a plea for 'everything right away'".

The centre-right, defeated in an upset June 1 election, promised resolute, but constructive opposition. Centrist UDF opposition floor leader Francois Bayrou said: "If what you say or do or are preparing to do appears harmful or to fall short, we will be determined to fight it."
Gaullist RPR floor leader Philippe Seguin, warning Jospin against using a planned audit of public finances as an excuse to go back on France's European commitments.
